title: Ratio, Proportion and Rates of Change

lessons.title: Share 20 in 2:3
lessons.label: Share 20 in 2:3
lessons.objective: Find equal parts before combining them into ratio shares.
prerequisites: Count small quantities and read the mathematical symbols used here.

curriculum.title: GCSE Mathematics 8300 — Ratio, Proportion and Rates of Change

tutorNotes.observe: Pause after each change. Ask the student to explain the picture before continuing.
tutorNotes.misconception: Dividing twenty by two and twenty by three separately.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: Why do we divide by five rather than by two or three?

steps.title: Start with the whole amount
steps.explanation: Share twenty counters in the ratio two to three.

steps.title: Count the equal parts
steps.explanation: We need five equal parts: two for A and three for B.

scene.description: Five equal parts, each containing four counters.

steps.title: Find the size of one part

left.text: twenty divided by five equals four
left.spoken: twenty divided by five equals four

steps.explanation: Twenty shared equally between five parts gives four in each part.

scene.description: Each of the five parts contains four.

steps.title: Give A two parts
steps.explanation: A gets two parts. Two groups of four make eight.

scene.description: The first two of five parts belong to A.

steps.title: Give B the other three parts
steps.explanation: B gets the other three parts. Three groups of four make twelve.

scene.description: A has eight and B has twelve; all twenty counters are used.

steps.title: Check the whole and the ratio
steps.explanation: Eight plus twelve is twenty. Eight to twelve simplifies to two to three.

scene.description: The final shares are eight and twelve.

lessons.title: Equivalent ratios
lessons.label: Equivalent ratios
lessons.objective: Explain why multiplying both parts by the same number preserves a ratio.
prerequisites: Count small quantities and read the mathematical symbols used here.

curriculum.title: GCSE Mathematics 8300 — Ratio, Proportion and Rates of Change

tutorNotes.observe: Pause after each change. Ask the student to explain the picture before continuing.
tutorNotes.misconception: Doubling only one part preserves a ratio.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: What would happen if we doubled A but left B unchanged?

steps.title: Start with two parts and three parts
steps.explanation: A has two counters for every three in B.

scene.description: Two A counters and three B counters.

steps.title: Double both groups

left.text: two times two to three times two
left.spoken: two times two to three times two

steps.explanation: Add one matching copy to each group. Both groups double together.

scene.description: Four A counters and six B counters. New copies have gold outlines.

steps.title: The relationship stays the same

left.text: two to three equals four to six
left.spoken: two to three equals four to six

steps.explanation: Four to six is equivalent to two to three. Each group is twice as large.

scene.description: The groups remain in the ratio two to three.

lessons.title: Simplify 6:9
lessons.label: Simplify 6:9
lessons.objective: Count equal bundles to simplify both parts of a ratio.
prerequisites: Count small quantities and read the mathematical symbols used here.

curriculum.title: GCSE Mathematics 8300 — Ratio, Proportion and Rates of Change

tutorNotes.observe: Pause after each change. Ask the student to explain the picture before continuing.
tutorNotes.misconception: Subtracting the same number from both parts preserves a ratio.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: Why must every bundle contain the same number of counters?

steps.title: Six counters and nine counters
steps.explanation: We want the same relationship using smaller whole numbers.

scene.description: Six A counters and nine B counters.

steps.title: Make bundles of three
steps.explanation: Put three counters in every bundle. A makes two bundles; B makes three.

scene.description: Two A bundles of three and three B bundles of three.

steps.title: Count bundles instead of counters

left.text: six divided by three to nine divided by three equals two to three
left.spoken: six divided by three to nine divided by three equals two to three

steps.explanation: Divide both counts by three. Two bundles to three bundles gives the simplest ratio.

scene.description: Each counter now represents one bundle of three.
scene.caption: Each displayed counter now represents one bundle.

lessons.title: Cost of five items
lessons.label: Cost of five items
lessons.objective: Find a unit cost, then scale it to the required number of identical items.
prerequisites: Count small quantities and read the mathematical symbols used here.

curriculum.title: GCSE Mathematics 8300 — Ratio, Proportion and Rates of Change

tutorNotes.observe: Pause after each change. Ask the student to explain the picture before continuing.
tutorNotes.misconception: Adding five to the original cost instead of finding an equal cost per item.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: Why does the unit cost stay the same when we buy five identical items?

steps.title: Three identical items cost twelve pounds
steps.explanation: The total cost is twelve pounds. Share it equally between three identical items.

scene.description: Twelve one-pound cards represent the total cost.
scene.caption: Each card represents one pound.

steps.title: Separate the equal costs

left.text: twelve pounds divided by three equals four pounds
left.spoken: twelve pounds divided by three equals four pounds

steps.explanation: Split the total into three equal costs. Each item costs four pounds.

scene.description: Three equal groups each contain four one-pound cards.
scene.caption: Each card represents one pound.

steps.title: Focus on one item
steps.explanation: The unit cost is four pounds. Keep this same cost for every item.

steps.title: Make five equal copies

left.text: five times four pounds equals twenty pounds
left.spoken: five times four pounds equals twenty pounds

steps.explanation: Five identical items cost five lots of four pounds: twenty pounds.

scene.description: Five groups of four one-pound cards total twenty pounds.
scene.caption: Each card represents one pound.
